key_insight: A hybrid AI model that combines mammogram images with patient clinical data can improve early breast cancer detection in low-resource settings.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support more accurate and context-aware breast cancer screening in settings with limited radiology expertise and fragmented records.
method: Transformer-based cross-modal attention fused mammogram and structured clinical data
Trained and validated on 2,560 mammograms from 1,024 patients across four Ethiopian referral hospitals
Compared against image-only baselines and assessed robustness on low-quality images
evidence_signal: The model achieved 97.8% accuracy, 97.2% sensitivity, 98.3% specificity, and an AUC of 0.987, with biopsy-confirmed labels and only 3.2% performance degradation on poor-quality images.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may require careful local validation to confirm performance across different populations, workflows, and data quality conditions.
paper_title: Hybrid Cross-Modal Attention Network for Early Breast Cancer Detection in Low-Resource Clinical Settings
